dedupe_keys.name: capital bikeshare station reallocation and rebalancing optimisation washington dc

description: This case study analyses how Capital Bikeshare in the Washington DC metropolitan area is used and proposes an optimisation for moving stations and bikes. Pedram Beigi, Michel Khoueiry, Mohammad Sadra Rajabi and Samer Hamdar of George Washington University note that the system had more than 4,300 bikes at 654 stations across seven jurisdictions, and that some stations are regularly empty or full because supply and demand are out of balance. They study the demand pattern from trip data and formulate a deterministic integer programme that reallocates stations daily and rebalances bikes, so operators can prepare overnight for the morning rush and for special events. Coverage: the Washington DC Capital Bikeshare network around 2021 and 2022. Access: arXiv preprint from April 2022; the underlying trip history is published by Capital Bikeshare. Licence and cost: free to read under the arXiv non-exclusive licence. Caveats: a conference-style preprint with a deterministic model, no stochastic demand or dockless vehicles, and no released code; outcomes are modelled, not operational results. It is a worked example of operations control and capacity planning for docked bike sharing, and relates to the Citi Bike system data record, a comparable public trip dataset in the catalogue.
